**The Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:** ﴿Nay, but they denied the Hour﴾, meaning the Resurrection, ﴿and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blazing fire﴾, meaning a fire kindled and blazing.

﴿When it sees them from a distant place﴾. Al-Kalbi and al-Suddi said: from a distance of a year's journey. It was also said: from a distance of a hundred years. And it was said: five hundred years. It is established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire between the two eyes of Hell." They said: "Does Hell have two eyes?" He said: "Yes. Have you not heard the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place﴾?" [[Al-Suyuti attributed it (6/238) to al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh. Al-Tabari transmitted it with the wording: "Whoever says about me what I did not say…" (18/187).]] It was also said: "When its guardians see them."

﴿They will hear its raging (taghayyuz) and its roaring (zafir)﴾. Taghayyuz means boiling, like an angry person whose chest boils with rage. Zafir means a sound. If it is asked: how can it hear raging? It is said: its meaning is that they saw and knew that it had raging, and they heard its roaring, as the poet said:

"And I saw your husband in the battle,
wearing a sword and a spear."

That is, carrying a spear. This is one interpretation. The second is that the verb "mutaqalladan" (wearing) is understood in the sense of "mutasallihan" (armed), and so the verse means: they heard it and saw its raging and roaring. Or the verb is understood in the sense of "adraku" (perceived), so that it includes both raging and roaring. See al-Bahr al-Muhit (6/485).

It was also said: they heard its raging, meaning the sound of the raging, from its blazing and kindling. ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: "Hell will exhale a single roar on the Day of Resurrection, and no angel brought near, nor any sent prophet, will remain except that he falls on his face."

Al-Farra' said: "al-raja'" (hope, expectation) here means fear, in the dialect of Tihama (a region in the Hijaz), and from it is the Exalted's saying: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not expect dignity from Allah?﴾ [Nuh: 13], meaning: you do not fear the greatness of Allah.

﴿Why have the angels not been sent down to us, or [why] do we not see our Lord?﴾ meaning: so that they may inform us that Muhammad is truthful, or so that He may inform us of that Himself.

﴿They have indeed been arrogant﴾, meaning: they have magnified themselves (taʿazzamū).

﴿within themselves﴾ by this statement, ﴿and have transgressed with great transgression﴾. Mujahid said: "ʿataw" means they exceeded the limits in speech, and "al-ʿutuww" is the most severe disbelief and the most vile wrongdoing. Their "ʿutuww" is their demand to see Allah in order that they may believe in Him.

﴿On the day they see the angels﴾ at the time of death. It is also said: on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿there will be no good tidings that day for the criminals﴾, meaning for the disbelievers. That is because the angels give good tidings to the believers on the Day of Resurrection, and say to the disbelievers: "There are no good tidings for you." This is what ʿAtiyyah said. Some of them said: its meaning is that there will be no good tidings for the criminals on the Day of Resurrection, that is, no glad tidings of Paradise for them, as the believers are given glad tidings.

﴿And they will say: "A forbidding, forbidden [barrier]"﴾. ʿAtaʾ related from Ibn ʿAbbas: The angels say: "A prohibition, a forbidden thing, [that] he should enter Paradise, except one who said: 'There is no god but Allah.'" Muqatil said: When the disbelievers come out of their graves, the angels say to them: "Forbidden and prohibited for you is that there should be glad tidings for you." Ibn Jurayj said: When the Arabs were overtaken by hardship and saw what they disliked, they said: "Hijran mahjuran" (a forbidding, forbidden [barrier]), and so they would say it when they saw the angels.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 25, verses 23–24:**

﴿And We will proceed﴾ (wa-'amadna, meaning "and We intended") ﴿to what they did of deeds, and make it scattered dust﴾. That is: void, with no reward. They did not do it for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Scholars differed about *al-haba'* (fine dust). Ali said: "It is what is seen in a window when the sunlight falls into it, like dust. It cannot be touched by hands, and it is not seen in shade." This is also the view of al-Hasan, Ikrimah and Mujahid. *Al-manthur* means "scattered."

Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is what the winds blow away and scatter of dust and crushed plant matter. Muqatil said: it is what rises from the hooves of animals when they travel. It was also said: "*al-haba' al-manthur*" is what is seen in a window, and "*al-haba' al-munbathth*" is what the winds scatter from the hooves of horses.

[[See these sayings in al-Tabari: 19/4–5; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/246; Zad al-Masir: 6/83. Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him (3/315), said: "The sum of these sayings is an indication of the meaning of the verse: they did deeds which they believed had some substance, but when they were presented to the King, the Judge, the Just, who does not oppress or wrong anyone, they turned out to be nothing at all. They are likened in this to a worthless, insignificant, scattered thing from which its owner can obtain nothing at all, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes, which the wind blows hard on a stormy day﴾." He also said: "He informs that these polytheists gain nothing from the deeds they thought would save them, because they lacked the legal condition: either sincerity in them, or following the law of Allah. Every deed that is not sincere and in accordance with the accepted Law is void. The deeds of the disbelievers cannot be free of one of these two defects, and sometimes they combine both, making them even further from acceptance."]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 25, verse 35–38:

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book and appointed with him his brother Aaron as a minister﴾ (wazīran), helping (mu'inan) and supporting (zahīran).

﴿So We said: "Go both of you to the people who denied Our signs"﴾ meaning the Copts, ﴿then We utterly destroyed them﴾ there is an implied element here, meaning: they denied the two of them, so We utterly destroyed them, ﴿a complete destruction﴾, We destroyed them with destruction.

﴿And the people of Noah, when they denied the messengers﴾, meaning the messenger. Whoever denies one messenger has denied all the messengers, and therefore it is mentioned in the plural form.

﴿We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind﴾, meaning: a lesson for those who come after them. ﴿And We have prepared for the wrongdoers﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿a painful punishment﴾, in addition to what befell them of the punishment in this world.

﴿And 'Ad and Thamud﴾, meaning: and We destroyed 'Ad and Thamud, ﴿and the companions of the Rass﴾. Scholars have differed about them. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: they were a people of a well, sitting beside it, and people of livestock, who worshipped idols. God sent to them Shu'ayb, calling them to Islam, but they persisted in their rebellion and in harming Shu'ayb, peace be upon him. While they were around the well in their dwellings, the well collapsed, and they were swallowed up along with their homes and their properties, and they all perished. "Rass" means a well, and every well that has not been lined with stones or baked brick is a rass. Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: "Rass" is a well at Falaj al-Yamamah; they killed their prophet, so God Almighty destroyed them. Some said: they are the remnant of Thamud, the people of Salih, and they are the people of the well which God mentioned in His saying: "And a well abandoned and a palace high-built" [al-Hajj: 45]. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they had a prophet called Handhalah ibn Safwan, and they killed him, so God Almighty destroyed them. Ka'b, Muqatil and al-Suddi said: "Rass" is a well at Antioch, in which they killed Habib the carpenter, and they are the ones God mentioned in Surah Ya-Sin. It was also said: they are the companions of the Trench (al-Ukhdud), and "Rass" is the trench they dug. 'Ikrimah said: they are a people who threw their prophet into a well [[The following opinions regarding the meaning of "companions of the Rass" have no firm evidence, and al-Tabari preferred that they are the companions of the Trench, and some of the preceding opinions are rejected by other texts, and God knows best. See: al-Tabari: 19/13-15; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/256-257; Zad al-Masir: 6/90; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 6/495-498; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/319-320.]]. It was also said: "Rass" is a mine, and its plural is ri sas.

﴿And generations between them, many﴾, meaning: and We destroyed many generations between 'Ad and the companions of the Rass.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 25, verse 48:**

﴿It is He who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy﴾, meaning the rain. ﴿And We send down from the sky pure water﴾. The word *tahur* (purifying, pure) is that which is pure in itself and purifies other things. It is a name for that by which one purifies oneself, just as *sahur* is a name for that with which one takes the pre-dawn meal (*tasahhur*), and *fatur* is a name for that with which one breaks the fast. The evidence for this is what we have related, that the Prophet ﷺ said concerning the sea: "Its water is pure (*tahur*), and its dead creatures are lawful." [[Related by Imam Malik in the Muwatta: 1/22; Abu Dawud in the chapter on performing ablution with sea water: 1/80; al-Tirmidhi in the chapter on what has come regarding sea water being pure: 1/224-225, and he said, "This is a hasan sahih hadith"; al-Nasai in Taharah: 1/50, 176; Ibn Majah in the chapter on ablution with sea water: 1/136, 137; al-Hakim authenticated it: 1/140; Ibn Hibban, no. 119; and Ibn Khuzaymah: 1/59. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/55.

Al-Tirmidhi said: I asked Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari about this hadith, and he said, "It is a sahih hadith." Al-Bayhaqi said: al-Bukhari and Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj did not include it in their Sahih only because of a disagreement over the names of Sa'id ibn Salamah and al-Mughirah ibn Abi Burdah. See Talkhis al-Habir: 1/9.]] By *tahur* he means *mutahhir* (purifying). Water is therefore purifying, because it purifies a person from minor ritual impurity (*hadath*) and from najasah (physical impurity). As He said in another verse: ﴿And He sends down on you water from the sky to purify you by it﴾ [al-Anfal: 11]. Thus it is established by this that purification is specific to water.

The people of opinion (*ashab al-ra'y*) held that *tahur* means *tahir* (pure in itself), to the extent that they permitted removing najasah with pure liquids such as vinegar, rose water, broth, and the like. [[Al-Jassas said in Ahkam al-Qur'an (5/201): "*Tahur*, in the form of an intensive description of it as pure and as purifying other things, so it is *tahir mutahhir*, just as one says *darub* and *qatul*, meaning one who strikes and one who kills, an intensive description of that attribute."]] If it were permissible to remove najasah with these, it would be permissible to remove hadath with them. Some scholars held that *tahur* is that from which purification is repeated, just as *sabur* is a name for one who repeatedly exercises patience (*sabr*), and *shakur* is a name for one who repeatedly gives thanks (*shukr*). This is the view of Malik, to the extent that he permitted performing ablution with water in which one had already performed ablution once. [[In al-Mudawwanah (1/4): "Malik said: One should not perform ablution with water with which one has already performed ablution once; he said: there is no good in it... I said: If a man finds no water except that with which someone has already performed ablution once, should he perform tayammum or perform ablution with that water? He said: Performing ablution with that water with which one has already performed ablution once is more beloved to me, if the water used is pure."]]

If something falls into water and changes its taste, colour, or smell, does its purifying quality (*tahuriyyah*) disappear? There is a distinction. If the thing that falls in is something that the water cannot be protected from, such as mud, dust, and tree leaves, the water's purifying quality does not disappear, so purification with it is permissible, just as when it changes from prolonged standing in its place. Likewise, if something falls into it that does not mix with it, such as oil poured into it, so that the water takes on its scent, purification with it is permissible, because its change is due to proximity, not to mixing. If the thing is something from which the water can be protected and which mixes with it, such as vinegar, saffron, or the like, the purifying quality disappears, so performing ablution with it is not permissible. If none of its attributes changes, one considers: if what falls into it is something pure whose falling does not remove its purifying quality, then purification with it is permissible, whether the water is little or much. If what falls into it is something impure (*najis*), one considers: if the water is less than two *qullatan*, it becomes najis; if it is two *qullatan* or more, it is pure, and performing ablution with it is permissible. The two *qullatan* are five *qirab*, and their weight is five hundred *ratl*. The evidence for this is what: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us, Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us, Abd al-Rahim ibn al-Muniyb informed us, Jarir informed us from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he was asked about water found in the desert and what beasts and predators come to it. He said: "When the water is two *qullatan*, it does not carry impurity (*khabath*)." [[Related by Abu Dawud in Taharah, chapter on what makes water najis: 1/56; al-Tirmidhi in the chapter on water not being made najis by anything: 1/215; al-Nasai in the chapter on the measure for water: 1/46; Ibn Majah in the chapter on the amount of water that does not become najis: 1/172; al-Darimi in Wudu: 1/187; Ibn Khuzaymah: 1/49; al-Shafi'i in al-Umm: 1/4; and Imam Ahmad: 2/27.]] This is the view of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Ishaq, and a group of the people of hadith: that when water reaches this limit, it does not become najis by the falling of najasah into it, so long as none of its attributes changes. [[For detail, see Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Awsat fi al-Sunan wa al-Ijma': 1/260 and following.]]

A group held that little water does not become najis by the falling of najasah into it, so long as its taste, colour, or smell does not change. This is the view of al-Hasan, Ata, al-Nakha'i, and al-Zuhri. They argued with what: Abu al-Qasim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi informed us, Abu al-Harith Tahir ibn Muhammad al-Tahiri informed us, Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim informed us, Abu al-Muwajjih Muhammad ibn Amr ibn al-Muwajjah informed us, Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl informed us, Abu Usamah informed us from al-Walid ibn Kathir, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Rafi' ibn Khadij, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri who said: It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, shall we perform ablution from the well of Bud'ah?" It is a well into which menstrual rags, dog flesh, and filth are thrown. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, water is pure; nothing makes it najis." [[Related by Abu Dawud in Taharah, chapter on what has come regarding the well of Bud'ah: 1/73; al-Tirmidhi in the chapter on water being pure and nothing making it najis: 1/203-205, and he said, "This is a hasan hadith. Abu Usamah has embellished this hadith, and no one has related the hadith of Abu Sa'id concerning the well of Bud'ah better than Abu Usamah narrated it. This hadith has been related through several other chains from Abu Sa'id." It was also related by al-Nasai in the chapter mentioning the well of Bud'ah: 1/174; Ibn Majah: 1/173; al-Shafi'i: 1/12 in the arrangement of the Musnad; al-Daraqutni: 1/13; Imam Ahmad: 3/31, 86; and al-Hakim authenticated it.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 25, verses 49–50:

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 25, verses 51–54:**

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Had We willed, We could have raised up in every town a warner﴾, a messenger who would warn them. But We sent you to all the towns, and We placed upon you the burden of warning all of them, so that by your patience in bearing it you would earn from Us the honour and the lofty rank that We have prepared for you.

﴿So do not obey the disbelievers﴾ in what they call you to, namely agreeing with them and flattering them (mudahanah).

﴿And strive against them with it﴾, that is, with the Qur'an, ﴿with a great striving﴾, a severe one.

﴿And it is He who let loose the two seas﴾: He mingled them and let one flow into the other. It was also said: He sent them along their courses and left them free, as horses are let loose in a pasture (marj). The root of "marj" is mixing and letting loose. It is said: "I let the animal loose (marajtu al-dabbah) and I set it loose in the pasture (amrajtuha), when I released it and left it to go wherever it wished." ﴿This one is sweet and fresh﴾, extremely sweet, and "furat" is the sweetest of waters. ﴿And this one is salty and bitter﴾, extremely salty. It was also said: ujaj means bitter. ﴿And He placed between them a barrier﴾, that is, a barrier by His power, so that the sweet does not mix with the salt nor the salt with the sweet. ﴿And a forbidding partition﴾, that is, a prohibited screen, so that they do not transgress and the salt does not corrupt the sweet.

﴿And it is He who created man from water﴾, from the sperm-drop (nutfah), ﴿and made him [a being of] lineage (nasab) and affinity (sihr)﴾, that is, He made him one possessing lineage and affinity. It was said: "nasab" is that whose marriage is forbidden, and "sihr" is that whose marriage is permitted. Thus nasab is what creates prohibition, and sihr is what does not create it. It was also said, and this is the sound view: nasab is kinship by blood, and sihr is the relationship by marriage that resembles kinship, and it is the cause that makes marriage forbidden. We have mentioned that God, exalted is He, forbade seven [women] by nasab and seven by sabab (cause of affinity), in His saying [[Related by Malik in Kitab al-Istisqa', chapter on seeking rain through the stars: 1/192; and al-Bukhari in al-Istisqa', chapter on God's saying: "And you make your provision that you deny" (56:82): 2/522, and in al-Salat, al-Maghazi and al-Tawhid; and Muslim in al-Iman, chapter on the disbelief of one who says "we were given rain by the nawʾ," no. (71): 1/83–84; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/419.]] "Forbidden to you are your mothers" (4:23). ﴿And your Lord is ever Competent﴾.

**Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful﴾**, meaning: the excellent of the servants. It was also said: this idafah (possessive construction) is for specification and distinction; otherwise, all of creation are servants of Allah.

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: they are people of dignity and chastity who do not behave foolishly; and if foolishness is directed at them, they respond with forbearance. The word "hawn" (humility) in the language means gentleness and softness [[See these statements in: al-Tabari, 19/33-34.]].

﴿And when the ignorant address them﴾, meaning the foolish, with what they dislike, ﴿they say, "Peace"﴾. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: speech by which they are safe from sin. Al-Hasan said: if an ignorant person acts ignorantly towards them, they show forbearance and do not respond in ignorance; and the intended meaning is not the common greeting of peace. It is also narrated from al-Hasan: its meaning is that they greet them with salam; his evidence is the words of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: "And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it and say, 'To us our deeds, and to you your deeds; peace be upon you'" [al-Qasas: 55]. Al-Kalbi and Abu al-'Aliyah said: this was before they were commanded to fight, and then the verse of fighting abrogated it (naskh, abrogation) [[Al-Tabari preferred this view: 3/32-33.]]. It is also narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri that when he recited this verse he said: "This describes their days." Then he recited ﴿And those who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing﴾ and said: "This describes their nights."

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 25, verses 64–67:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And those who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing﴾. It is said of whoever reaches the night: "baat" (he spent the night), whether he sleeps or does not sleep. It is said: "baata fulanun qalaqan" (so-and-so spent the night restless). The meaning is: they spend the night before their Lord in prayer, ﴿prostrating﴾ upon their faces, and ﴿standing﴾ upon their feet. Ibn Abbas said: "Whoever prays two rak'ahs (units of prayer) or more after the final night prayer ('isha') has spent the night for Allah prostrating and standing." [[See: Majma' al-Zawa'id: 2 / 231.]] 

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us; Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us; Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani informed us; Humayd ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us; Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Uthman ibn Hakim, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Amrah, from Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever prays the 'isha' in congregation, it is as if he stood (in prayer) for half the night, and whoever prays the subh (dawn prayer) in congregation, it is as if he prayed the whole night." [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Mosques, chapter on the virtue of the 'isha' and subh prayers in congregation, no. (656): 1 / 454, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2 / 231.]]

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And those who say: "Our Lord, turn away from us the punishment of Hell; indeed its punishment is ever-clinging (gharaman)"﴾. So it was revealed: "And those who do not invoke with Allah another god" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir, Surah al-Furqan: 8/494, and Muslim in Iman, chapter on Islam erasing what came before it, no. (122): 1/113, and in Tafsir, no. (19): 4/2318. See also: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. (386).]].

﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit fornication﴾. And it was revealed: "Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah" [al-Zumar: 53].

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) related to us, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id related to us, Jarir related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from Amr ibn Shurahbil, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest in the sight of Allah?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you." He said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child out of fear that he will share your food." He said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with the wife of your neighbour." So Allah revealed its confirmation: "And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit fornication; and whoever does that will meet a penalty (athaman)" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir of Surah al-Furqan, chapter "And those who do not invoke with Allah another god": 8/492.]]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And whoever does that﴾ — i.e., any of these deeds, ﴿will meet a penalty (athaman)﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: It means the recompense of sin (ithm). Abu ʿUbaydah said: "al-atham" means punishment. Mujahid said: "al-atham" is a valley in Hell, narrated from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs [[See: al-Tabari 19/44-45; this is also the view of Mujahid and ʿIkrimah. See also: al-Zuhd of the Imam Hannad: 1/369 with the editor's note.]]. And it is narrated in a hadith: "al-Ghayy and al-Athnam are two wells into which the pus of the people of the Fire flows" [[Narrated by al-Tabari from the hadith of Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him, at length: 19/44-45.]].

﴿يُضَاعَفْ لَهُ الْعَذَابُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ مُهَانًا﴾ [Punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide in it in humiliation.] Ibn 'Amir and Abu Bakr read "yuḍā'afu" and "yakhludu" with a *ḍammah* on the *fā'* and the *dāl*, as a nominal beginning (*ibtidā'*, a sentence beginning a new clause). Ibn 'Amir also read "yuḍa''ifu" with a shaddah on the *ḍād*. The others read them with a *jazm* (the jussive vowel, a final vowel elided by apocope) on the *fā'* and the *dāl*, as the answer of the conditional (*jawāb al-sharṭ*).

﴿إِلَّا مَنْ تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًا صَالِحًا﴾ [Except for one who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds.] Qatadah said: "Except for one who repents from his sin, believes in his Lord, and does righteous deeds in what is between him and his Lord." Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us; al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah informed me; Musa ibn Muhammad narrated to us; Musa ibn Harun al-Hammal narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Shafi'i narrated to us; 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, on the authority of 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar, on the authority of 'Ali ibn Yazid, on the authority of Yusuf ibn Mihran, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "We read it in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for two years: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity⦆ [the verse], then there was revealed: ﴿except for one who repents⦆. I never saw the Prophet ﷺ rejoice at anything as much as he rejoiced at it, and at His saying: 'Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you your past and future sins'" [[Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/84): "Al-Tabarani narrated it through 'Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Yusuf ibn Mihran. Both are deemed trustworthy but have some weakness, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy. There is a hadith in the Sahih other than this one." al-Suyuti added its attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh. al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/279.]] (Al-Fath 1–2). ﴿Then those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful⦆.

A group held that this replacement occurs in this world. Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Mujahid, al-Suddi, and al-Dahhak said: Allah replaces their foul deeds of polytheism with fine deeds of Islam: He replaces polytheism with faith, the killing of believers with the killing of polytheists, and fornication with chastity and marital protection [[See: al-Tabari: 19/46–47.]]. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 25, verse 71:

His statement, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous deeds﴾. Some of the scholars (ahl al-'ilm) said: this refers to repentance from other than what was mentioned in the first verse, namely killing and fornication. That is: whoever repents from polytheism (shirk) and does righteous deeds, i.e., performs the obligatory duties (al-fara'id), among those who have not killed and have not committed fornication. ﴿Then indeed he turns back to Allah﴾, i.e., he returns to Him after death, ﴿with a good return﴾, by which he is preferred over others who killed and committed fornication. So the first repentance, which is His saying "and whoever repents," is a turning away from polytheism, and the second is a return to Allah for recompense and reward.

Some of them said: this verse also refers to repentance from all evil deeds (sayyi'at). Its meaning is: whoever intends repentance and resolves upon it, let him repent for the sake of Allah's countenance. His saying ﴿turns back to Allah﴾ is a report with the meaning of a command, i.e., let him turn back to Allah. It was also said: its meaning is that he should know that his repentance and his final return are to Allah.

﴿Those who do not witness falsehood﴾. Al-Dahhak and most of the exegetes said: it means shirk (associating partners with God)[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 19/48, and by Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of al-Dahhak. Al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/378.]]. Ali ibn Talhah said: it means bearing false witness (shahadat al-zur)[[Ali ibn Talhah]]. Umar ibn al-Khattab used to flog a false witness forty lashes, blacken his face, and parade him through the marketplace[[Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 8/326 and 327, and by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 10/142.]]. Ibn Juraij said: it means lying[[Al-Tabari: 19/49; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/282.]]. Mujahid said: it means the festivals of the polytheists[[This is what al-Khatib narrated from Ibn Abbas. Al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/282.]]. It was also said: it means wailing (al-nawh)[[This is narrated from al-Hasan. Al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/283.]]. Qatadah said: they do not support the people of falsehood in their falsehood[[Narrated by Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim, as in al-Durr: 6/283.]]. Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: they do not witness idle amusement and singing[[Narrated by Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim, as in al-Durr: 6/283.]]. Ibn Mas'ud said: "Singing produces hypocrisy in the heart just as water produces plants"[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan as a statement of Ibn Mas'ud: 10/223, and in al-Shu'ab as a marfu' report from Jabir. Abd al-Razzaq narrated the first part of it from Ibrahim in al-Musannaf: 11/4. Ibn Hajar said in Talkhis al-Habir (4/199): Abu Dawud narrated it without the simile, and al-Bayhaqi narrated it from Ibn Mas'ud as marfu', with an unnamed narrator in its chain; al-Bayhaqi also narrated it as mawquf. There is a report on the subject from Abu Hurayrah, narrated by Ibn Adi. Ibn Tahir said: the soundest chain on this matter is that it is the statement of Ibrahim. Al-Albani, in his commentary on al-Mishkat: 3/1355, attributed it to Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Dhamm al-Malahi with a weak chain. See also al-Fawa'id al-Majmu'ah of al-Shawkani, p. 254, and Kashf al-Khafa: 2/103.]]. The root of "zur" is making something appear good and describing it contrary to its reality; it is the disguising of falsehood with what gives the impression that it is true[[Al-Tabari commented after this: (19/49) "Shirk may enter into this, because it makes its adherents appear good, so that they even think it is true, when it is false. Singing also enters into it, because it too is made appealing by the trilling of the voice, so that the listener finds his hearing of it sweet. Lying also may enter into it, since its speaker makes it appear good, so that the listener thinks it is true. All of these fall within the meaning of zur. Given this, the most correct interpretation is to say: 'those who do not witness any falsehood, neither shirk, nor singing, nor lying, nor anything else, and everything to which the name zur applies,' because God's description of them, that they do not witness zur, is general, so nothing should be specified from it except by a proof that must be accepted, whether a report or reason."]]. ﴿And when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity﴾. Muqatil said: when they hear insults and harm from the disbelievers, they turn away and overlook them. This is the narration of Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid, and its parallel is His saying: "And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it" (al-Qasas: 55)[[Al-Tabari commented after this: 3/32-33 — the same passage as above, in full.]]. Al-Suddi said: this verse is abrogated (mansukhah) by the verse of fighting[[The term "mansukh" (abrogated) refers to a ruling whose validity has been removed by a later revealed ruling (naskh).]]. Al-Hasan and al-Kalbi said: "idle talk" means all sins, meaning that when they pass by a gathering of amusement and falsehood, they pass by it quickly, turning away, in dignity. It is said: so-and-so was dignified (takarrama) regarding what disgraces him when he kept himself pure of it and honored himself by avoiding it[[See also al-Tabari's interpretation and his preference: 19/50.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 25, verses 73–74:

﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the signs of their Lord, do not fall down﴾ — they do not fall or collapse, ﴿upon them deaf and blind﴾ — as if they were deaf and blind. Rather, they hear what they are reminded of and understand it, and they see the truth in it and follow it. Al-Qutaybi [[See: al-Qurtayn by Ibn Mutarrif: 2/51–52.]] said: they do not pretend to be heedless of them, as if they had not heard them, deaf, and as if they had not seen them, blind.

﴿And those who say: Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and our offspring﴾ — Abu 'Amr, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read it without an alif (as dhurriyyatina, singular form). The rest read it with an alif, in the plural. ﴿The coolness of our eyes﴾ — that is, righteous, pious children, who say: make them righteous so that our eyes may be gladdened by that. Al-Qurazi said: nothing is more pleasing to the eye of a believer than to see his wife and children obedient to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Al-Hasan also said this. The word "qurrah" is in the singular because it is a verbal noun (masdar). Its origin is from coolness (al-bard), because the Arabs suffer from heat and find relief in coolness. The "coolness of the eye" is mentioned at times of joy, and the "heat of the eye" at times of grief. It is said: the tear of the eye at joy is cool, and at grief it is hot. Al-Azhari said: the meaning of "coolness of the eyes" is that one's heart meets with one whom he is pleased with, so that his eye is cooled by him from looking at anyone else.

﴿And make us leaders for the righteous﴾ — that is, imams whom they follow in goodness through us. He did not say "a'immah" (plural); as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, we are a messenger of the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 16]. It is also said he meant "a'immah," as in His saying: "Indeed, they are an enemy to me" [al-Shu'ara: 77], meaning "enemies." And it is said: "Amirna ha'ula'" (these are our commanders), meaning "our commanders." It is also said: it is a masdar like al-siyam and al-qiyam; it is said: "amma imaman," just as it is said: "qama qiyaman" and "sama siyaman." Al-Hasan said: we follow the righteous, and the righteous follow us. Ibn 'Abbas said: make us guiding imams, as He said: "And We made them imams guiding by Our command" [al-Sajdah: 24], and do not make us imams of misguidance, as He said: "And We made them imams calling to the Fire" [al-Qasas: 41]. It is also said: this is an inversion (maqlub), meaning: make the righteous a leader for us, and make us followers of them. This is the saying of Mujahid.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath informed us, my father informed us, al-A'mash informed us, Muslim narrated to us, from Masruq, who said: Abdullah said: Five have passed: the smoke, the moon, the Romans, the assault, and the inevitable [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of the Tafsir of Surat al-Furqan, chapter: "So it will be inevitable": 8 / 496, and Muslim in the Book of the Attributes of the Hypocrites and their Rulings, chapter on the smoke, no. (2798): 4 / 2157.]] ﴿So it will be inevitable﴾. It is also said: al-lizam (the inevitable) is the punishment of the Hereafter.

﴿Those will be rewarded﴾, meaning they will be given reward, ﴿with the lofty chamber﴾, meaning the high rank in Paradise. The word "ghurfah" (chamber) refers to any elevated, lofty building. Ata said: It means chambers of pearl, emerald and ruby in Paradise. ﴿For what they endured﴾, meaning for their patience in obeying God's command and in His worship. It is also said: for their patience in bearing the harm of the polytheists. And it is said: for their patience in restraining from desires. ﴿And they will be met therein﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr recited it as "yulaqqawna" with a fatha on the ya' and a light qaf, as in His saying: "So they will meet Ghayy" [Maryam: 59]. The others recited it with a damma on the ya' and a shadda on the qaf, as in His saying: "And He will give them radiance and joy" [al-Insan: 11]. As for His saying ﴿greeting﴾, it means sovereignty. It is also said: enduring everlasting life. ﴿And peace﴾, meaning that some of them greet others with peace. Al-Kalbi said: some of them greet one another with peace, and the Lord sends peace to them. It is also said: "salaman" means safety from calamities.

﴿Abiding therein; how excellent a place of settlement and dwelling﴾, meaning a place of residence and abode.

﴿Say: My Lord would not care for you﴾. Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: meaning, what would He do with you or how would He treat you. Abu Ubaydah said: it is said, "I did not give him any weight," meaning I did not count him, so his existence and his non-existence are the same. Its figurative sense is: what weight and what value do you have with Him. ﴿Were it not for your calling upon Him﴾, that is, your invoking Him. It is also said: were it not for your faith. It is also said: were it not for your worship. It is also said: were it not for His calling you to Islam; when you believe, your worth becomes apparent to you. Some people said: its meaning is: Say, my Lord would not care for your creation, were it not for your worship and obedience to Him, meaning that He created you for His worship, as He said: "I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me" [al-Dhariyat: 56]. This is the view of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. Some people said: "Say: He would not care" means He would not care for your forgiveness, were it not for your invoking, together with Him, other gods; or He would not do anything with your punishment, were it not for your polytheism, as God Most High said: ﴿What would God do with your punishment if you were thankful and believed?﴾ [al-Nisa': 147]. It is also said: He would not care for your punishment were it not for your calling upon Him in times of hardship, as He said: "But when they board the ship, they call upon God" [al-Ankabut: 65], and He said: "So We seized them with misfortune and adversity that they might humble themselves" [al-An'am: 42]. It is also said: "Say: My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication" means: I did not create you while I have any need of you, except that you ask Me and I give you, and you seek My forgiveness and I forgive you.

﴿Surely you have denied﴾, O disbelievers, addressing the people of Makkah, meaning: when God called you through the Messenger to His tawhid and His worship, you denied the Messenger and did not respond to him.

﴿So it will be inevitable﴾. This is His threat to them, meaning: your denial will be inevitable. Ibn Abbas said: death. Abu Ubaydah said: destruction. Ibn Zayd said: fighting. The meaning is: denial will be binding upon whoever denied, so he will not be granted repentance until he is recompensed for his deeds. Ibn Jarir [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 19 / 56-57.]] said: a lasting, binding punishment and a lingering destruction that will overtake some of you with others. They differed regarding it.
